form.label: DEI Help
form.description: Manual guidance for the complete detection engineering workflow.

header.p: Use this page when you need more detail than the interactive tutorial provides. Follow the lifecycle in order or open the section for the task you are performing.

div.p: Run Environment Discovery before building. Confirm indexes, sourcetypes, field availability, data freshness, and whether Enterprise Security is available.

ol.li: Resolve field gaps before treating a recommendation as production ready.
Use MITRE Coverage to confirm the behavior and technique mapping.

div.p: Evidence created: telemetry inventory, readiness state, field validation, and ATT&CK coverage context.
Select a scan-supported recommendation in Guided Detection Builder. Generate the draft, then verify the SPL, schedule guidance, MITRE ID, tactic, description, and required result fields.
Generated SPL is a starting point. Confirm index and sourcetype constraints match the deployed environment and remove logic that is not supported by observed data.

ol.li: Confirm an expected positive case matches.
Confirm a known benign or negative case does not.
Check result volume, runtime, required fields, and time bounds.
Repair syntax, field, or command errors and rerun validation.

div.p: Validation evidence belongs to the exact analytic version and does not carry forward after tuning.

The submission note should describe analytic intent, expected analyst behavior, validation evidence, known limitations, and operational ownership. A reviewer other than the submitter should verify logic, source coverage, fields, time bounds, schedule, suppression, response actions, ATT&CK mapping, and rollback.

summary.strong: Deploy and record the exact object

div.p: Deploy through the organization’s normal change process. Verify owner, app context, schedule, earliest/latest time, enablement state, throttling, actions, annotations, and rollback.

ul.li: Splunk saved searches: Settings → Searches, Reports, and Alerts.
Enterprise Security: Configure → Content → Content Management.

div.p: Record the exact saved-search or detection object name in DEI; a friendly label is not sufficient audit evidence.
Use real evidence from scheduler/search history, Job Inspector, source-data freshness, analyst dispositions, and downstream findings, notables, or risk events.
Zero results can be healthy, but document why zero was expected and how data availability was verified. For degraded or failing health, identify the owner and corrective action.
Do not tune simply because the option is available. Use: observed problem; supporting evidence; proposed change; measurable expected result; rollback condition.

Tuning can change SPL, thresholds, time windows, schedules, allowlists, suppression or throttling, risk settings, or response actions. Start a new version, revalidate, repeat peer review, redeploy, and return to monitoring.

Confirm a replacement detection or formally accept the coverage gap. Record the reason, owner, date, and retained evidence. Retiring the DEI lifecycle record does not disable the actual Splunk saved search; disable or remove that external object through change control.

ul.li: If a tutorial target is unavailable, complete the visible lifecycle action and restart the guide from Home.
If generated SPL fails, review the validation resolution, repair the SPL, and rerun validation.
If current telemetry is missing, rerun Environment Discovery and confirm search permissions and source freshness.
If a page appears stale after an upgrade, reload Splunk Web after the app restart and confirm the installed app version.
